To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intermittent preventive treatment (IPT) of malaria in children with sulphadoxine pyremethamine plus amodiaquine was associated with a modest increase in the risk of malaria in the subsequent transmission season.

intermittent preventive treatment of childhood malaria in Burkina Fosa with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine was associated with a higher risk of malaria in the following year, and that this was associated with a greater risk of malaria infection but not with a higher prevalence of anaemia, wasting or stunting.

intermittent preventive treatment of children (IPTi) with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTi-SP) was not associated with an increase or decrease in the incidence of severe malaria in children in Burkina Foso.

the use of SP+AQ as IPTc was associated with a modest increase in the risk of clinical malaria in children during the subsequent malaria transmission.
